text:
ada: Heads-up — finished attention kernel sweeps (Flash variants, paged-attn, fused-attn) across A100 / H100 / L40S. Found a weird perf regression at long seqs. Need quick triage.

ken: Nice. Which workloads? seq len range / batch sizes?

ada: Seq sweep: 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192. Batch sweep: 1, 2, 4, 8. For each GPU ran both decode (KV cache) and full-attn (no cache). Configs: FP16, 8-bit quantized variants for L40S.

marie: Any NVTX traces or perf counters? :eyes:

ada: Yep attached inline below — summarized numbers first (median tokens/sec). Perf-bot posted full CSV.

perf-bot: SUMMARY: A100 | H100 | L40S — flash-v1, flash-v2, paged-attn, fused-attn. Key finding: flash-v2 outperforms on short seqs (<=1024) across all GPUs. At seq=4096/8192, paged-attn shows stable memory but flash-v2 throughput drops ~18% on H100 decode path when batch>=4.

ryan: 18% on H100 decode path? That's surprising — did kernel selection fallback to a non-fused kernel at that point?

ada: I checked selection logs — runtime picked flash-v2 for the compute kernels but switched to a generic matmul fallback for KV gather when KV pages > threshold. That fallback is causing stalls.

ken: Can you paste the exact kernel flags / heuristic thresholds used?

ada: Sure. here's the bench command we used:

```bash
./bench_attention --model gpt-like --gpu A100,H100,L40S --seqs 256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192 
  --batches 1,2,4,8 --mode decode,full-attn --kernels flashv1,flashv2,paged,fused 
  --quant none,8bit --repeat 5 --nvtx
```

ada: Kernel selection heuristic (current):
- prefer fused if batch*seq <= 512k tokens and kv_pages < 4
- prefer flashv2 for seq <= 1024 if free_mem > 12GB
- fallback to generic matmul if kv_pages >= 4 or kv_page_hits low

marie: where kv_pages comes from? our paged-kv split size?

ada: kv_pages = ceil(kv_bytes / page_size) — page_size default 128MB. With long seq and batch >=4 kv_bytes crosses 512MB => 4 pages. On H100 the memory allocator fragmentation made actual contiguous free < page_size so runtime conservatively falls back.

sasha: Do we have NVLINK/PCIe differences affecting this? L40S with larger host mem looked fine?

ada: L40S behaved different — its allocator returned larger contiguous blocks so paged-attn stayed stable. H100's driver had more fragmentation in our test harness (CUDA 12.1 vs 12.3 differences).

ryan: Can you paste a short CSV excerpt? just the troubling lines for seq 8192, batch 4/8 across GPUs and kernels.

ada: PASTE CSV snippet:

"gpu,seq,batch,kernel,mode,median_tok_s,mem_used_mb"
"A100,8192,4,flashv2,decode,320,31240"
"A100,8192,4,paged,decode,410,28500"
"H100,8192,4,flashv2,decode,260,31800"
"H100,8192,4,paged,decode,395,29020"
"L40S,8192,4,flashv2,decode,360,30500"
"L40S,8192,4,paged,decode,380,29200"

ada: Note H100 flashv2 at 260 tok/s vs paged 395 tok/s — big gap. On A100 the gap exists but smaller.

ken: So paged-attn is actually faster at long seqs because it avoids the KV fallback fragmentation cost?

ada: Exactly. Paged-attn trades compute for more streaming I/O but keeps KV management cheap and avoids the matmul fallback.

marie: Any profiler flamegraphs?

ada: NVPROF/NVTX traces attached to perf-bot. Quick flame: time spent stalled in memcpy + generic_matmul kernel on H100 flash path.

perf-bot: ATTACHMENTS: nvtx_trace_h100_8192_batch4.zip (link), csv_full_results_1752003456.csv (link)

ryan: This suggests heuristics need to prefer paged-attn when kv_pages>=3 on H100. Also we should tune page_size lower for H100 tests (64MB) to reduce fragmentation hits.

ken: Agreed. Also consider retrying allocation with a temporary compaction or try smaller contiguous allocations before falling back. Maybe don't fall back immediately to generic matmul — try paged-attn first.

ada: I ran an experiment lowering page_size to 64MB on H100:
"H100,8192,4,flashv2,decode,300,31500"
"H100,8192,4,paged,decode,410,28800"
Better but still paged leads.

sasha: Could quantized kernels be less sensitive? 8-bit on L40S looked close. How about H100 8-bit?

ada: 8-bit reduced memory and improved flashv2 by ~10% at seq=8192 on H100 (flashv2 290 tok/s) but paged still ~395.

marie: Root cause action items?

ada: Proposed next steps: 1) change kernel selection heuristic: prefer paged-attn when kv_pages >= 3 for decode path on H100; 2) add allocation retry path to try smaller page_size / compaction before falling back; 3) add runtime flag to force paged vs flash for canary; 4) schedule a longer stability run (24h) to detect intermittent fragmentation; 5) file regression ticket with NV driver team (possible allocator behavior change between CUDA versions).

ryan: +1 on the heuristic toggle and force-flag. Can you open a canary with --force-paged for the top customers on Dedicated? Want to see production effect.

ada: Will do. Also adding a perf test to CI targeting seq 4096/8192 with batch 4 to catch regressions.

ken: I'll own the runtime change for the heuristic and allocation retry. Filing PR today.

ada: Thanks — I'll attach the full traces and PR link once ready. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: NOTE: last run stats stored at s3://redwood-perf/attention/1752003456/ — retention 90d.

ryan: Great work all. Follow-up sync tomorrow 10am PT?

ada: Works for me.
